issuer: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
title: New Mexico TRD Ruling 495-97-1 Withholding Agent and Investment Credit Act
text:
Ruling 495-97-1
Issued: April 10, 1997
Effective: April 10, 1997
A ruling has been requested concerning the applicability of certain provisions of the
Investment Credit Act, NMSA 1978, Sections 7-9A-1 (1995 Repl. Pamp.), to the following
facts:
X is a corporation doing business in New Mexico. X has carried on a
manufacturing operation in New Mexico in facilities consisting of real
property, improvements and equipment that are owned by a New Mexico
political subdivision and leased to X under the authority of an industrial
revenue bond. In the course of its business, X has applied for and been
granted approval of investment credits on equipment used in its
manufacturing operation.
X has formed a new corporation, Y, in a corporate reorganization. X has
contributed to Y all of its rights, title and interest in the property used in New
Mexico's manufacturing operation. Y will carry on the manufacturing
operations in New Mexico using the same property and employees that were
previously used by X. As part of the reorganization, X applied for and was
granted authority to act as withholding agent for Y under the provisions of
Internal Revenue Code § 3504.
As Y's authorized withholding agent, X will control the payment of wages
and remit the payment of withholding tax for all of Y's employees. Under the
provisions of IRC § 3504, X will be equally liable with Y for payment of
employment tax on Y's employees, including interest and penalties, if
applicable.
X asks whether it may apply its approved, but unused, investment credits against
withholding tax X pays on behalf of Y as Y's withholding agent.
Section 7-9A-8(A) of the Investment Credit Act allows “a taxpayer” who has
applied for and been granted investment credits to claim those credits against “the taxpayer's
compensating tax, gross receipts tax or withholding tax due to the state of New Mexico”.
The issue to be determined is whether X, the taxpayer who has been granted investment
credits, may apply those credits against Y's state withholding tax liability.
Section 7-3-2(C) of the Withholding Tax Act defines “employer” to include “a
person, or an officer, agent or employee of that person, having control of the payment of
wages...”.
Section 7-3-11(A) provides:
When a fiduciary, agent or other person has the control, receipts, custody or
disposal of or pays the wages of an employee or group of employees
employed by one or more employers and the fiduciary, agent or other person

has been designated by the United States secretary of the treasury to perform
such acts as required of employers for federal withholding purposes under
the Internal Revenue Code, the fiduciary, agent or other person shall perform
the acts required of employers by the provisions of the Withholding Tax Act.
All provisions of Chapter 7 NMSA 1978 applicable in respect to an
employer shall be applicable to a fiduciary, agent, or other person so
designated, but the employer, unless provided otherwise by law, for whom
the fiduciary, agent or other person acts shall remain subject to the
provisions of Chapter 7 NMSA 1978 applicable to employers.
The Withholding Tax Act treats any person with control over the payment of wages,
including a person designated as a withholding agent under IRC § 3504, as an employer
liable for payment of withholding tax. When X pays withholding tax on wages paid to Y's
employees, X is satisfying its own, as well as Y's, liability for payment of tax. This meets
the requirement in Section 7-9A-8(A) that a taxpayer holding investment credits claim those
credits against “the taxpayer's ... withholding tax due to the state of New Mexico”.
X may apply its approved, but unused, investment credits against withholding tax X
pays on behalf of Y.
